import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Exponential
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Trigonometric
import Mathlib.Tactic.Polyrith
/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simp]
def phaseShiftMatrix (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.mk_one, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',

C1_dependencies.name: Fin.isValue
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Simplification procedure for ensuring `Fin n` literals are normalized. -/
builtin_dsimproc [simp, seval] isValue ((OfNat.ofNat _ : Fin _)) := fun e => do
  let_expr OfNat.ofNat _ m _ ← e | return .continue
  let some ⟨n, v⟩ ← getFinValue? e | return .continue
  let some m ← getNatValue? m | return .continue
  if m < n then
    -- Design decision: should we return `.continue` instead of `.done` when simplifying.
    -- In the symbolic evaluator, we must return `.done`, otherwise it will unfold the `OfNat.ofNat`
    return .done e
  return .done <| toExpr v

C0_dependencies.name: phaseShiftMatrix

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/

  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

  added phases. -/

    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j

    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Exponential
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Trigonometric
import Mathlib.Tactic.Polyrith
/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simp]
def phaseShiftMatrix (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.mk_one, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',
    cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, star_def, ← exp_conj,
    _root_.map_mul, conj_I, conj_ofReal, neg_mul, ofReal_neg, mul_neg, Fin.mk_one, cons_val_one,
    head_fin_const, star_zero, head_cons, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd,
    tail_val', head_val', tail_cons, Fin.reduceFinMk, map_eq_zero]
  · rfl
  · rfl

/-- The multiple of two phase shift matrices is equal to the phase shift matrix with
  added phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_mul (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, mul_apply, cons_val', empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, cons_val_zero, vecCons_const, Fin.sum_univ_three, cons_val_one, head_cons,
    head_fin_const, mul_zero, add_zero, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons,
    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the unitary matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ⟨phaseShiftMatrix a b c,
  by
    rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
    change _ * (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = 1
    rw [phaseShiftMatrix_star, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← phaseShiftMatrix_one]
    simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, add_neg_cancel, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]⟩

/-- The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
  phase-shift matrix. -/
lemma phaseShift_coe_matrix (a b c : ℝ) : ↑(phaseShift a b c) = phaseShiftMatrix a b c := rfl

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix]
  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is an equivalence relation. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

/-- Two CKM matrices are equal if their underlying unitary matrices are equal. -/
lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

/-- The `ud`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ud_element) "[" V "]ud" => V.1 0 0

/-- The `us`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := us_element) "[" V "]us" => V.1 0 1

/-- The `ub`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ub_element) "[" V "]ub" => V.1 0 2

/-- The `cd`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cd_element) "[" V "]cd" => V.1 1 0

/-- The `cs`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cs_element) "[" V "]cs" => V.1 1 1

/-- The `cb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cb_element) "[" V "]cb" => V.1 1 2

/-- The `td`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := td_element) "[" V "]td" => V.1 2 0

/-- The `ts`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ts_element) "[" V "]ts" => V.1 2 1

/-- The `tb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := tb_element) "[" V "]tb" => V.1 2 2

/-- The setoid of CKM matrices defined by phase shifts of fermions. -/
instance CKMMatrixSetoid : Setoid CKMMatrix := ⟨PhaseShiftRelation, phaseShiftRelation_equiv⟩

/-- The matrix obtained from `V` by shifting the phases of the fermions. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShiftApply (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) : CKMMatrix :=
    phaseShift a b c * ↑V * phaseShift d e f

namespace phaseShiftApply

/-- A CKM matrix is equivalent to a phase-shift of itself. -/
lemma equiv (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    V ≈ phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f := by
  symm
  use a, b, c, d, e, f
  rfl

/-- The `ud` component of the CKM matrix obtained after applying a phase shift. -/
lemma ud (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f).1 0 0 = cexp (a * I + d * I) * V.1 0 0 := by
  simp only [Fin.isValue, phaseShiftApply_coe]
  rw [mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_three]
  rw [mul_apply, mul_apply, mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_three, Fin.sum_univ_three, Fin.sum_univ_three]
  simp only [Fin.isValue, cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const,
    cons_val_one, head_cons, zero_mul, add_zero, cons_val_two, tail_cons, head_fin_const, mul_zero,
    tail_val', head_val']
  change _ + _ * _ * 0 = _

/-- The `us` component of the CKM matrix obtained after applying a phase shift. -/
lemma us (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f).1 0 1 = cexp (a * I + e * I) * V.1 0 1 := by
  simp only [Fin.isValue, phaseShiftApply_coe]
  rw [mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_three]

  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0

  intro h

  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]

  intro hUV hVW

  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW

  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm

/-- Simplification procedure for ensuring `Fin n` literals are normalized. -/
builtin_dsimproc [simp, seval] isValue ((OfNat.ofNat _ : Fin _)) := fun e => do
  let_expr OfNat.ofNat _ m _ ← e | return .continue
  let some ⟨n, v⟩ ← getFinValue? e | return .continue
  let some m ← getNatValue? m | return .continue
  if m < n then
    -- Design decision: should we return `.continue` instead of `.done` when simplifying.
    -- In the symbolic evaluator, we must return `.done`, otherwise it will unfold the `OfNat.ofNat`
    return .done e
  return .done <| toExpr v

rag.content:
/-- Permuting rows and columns with two equivalences does not change the absolute value of the
determinant. -/
@[simp]
theorem abs_det_submatrix_equiv_equiv {R : Type*} [LinearOrderedCommRing R]
    (e₁ e₂ : n ≃ m) (A : Matrix m m R) :
    |(A.submatrix e₁ e₂).det| = |A.det| := by
  have hee : e₂ = e₁.trans (e₁.symm.trans e₂) := by ext; simp
  rw [hee]
  show |((A.submatrix id (e₁.symm.trans e₂)).submatrix e₁ e₁).det| = |A.det|
  rw [Matrix.det_submatrix_equiv_self, Matrix.det_permute', abs_mul, abs_unit_intCast, one_mul]

informal_proof:
First, we consider a representative \( M \) of an equivalence class of CKM matrices. The `ud`th element of \( M \), denoted as \( M_{ud} \), is of interest. 

Given the properties of CKM matrices, specifically their unitarity, the absolute value of \( M_{ud} \) is determined by the formal definition \( VudAbs \), which aligns with \( VAbs 0 0 \) when \( M \) is normalized and falls within the specified equivalence class.

Using Lean's `simp` tactic, we simplify \( VudAbs \) by applying definitions and properties related to CKM matrices and matrix representatives. The `simp_all` commands systematically reduce the expression, applying lemmas and rules such as `udApi`, `udAp`, and others, which handle specific transformations on matrix elements.

Each application of `simp_all` step-by-step refines \( VudAbs \) until it matches \( VAbs 0 0 \), thereby proving the equivalence. This process leverages the inherent structure and symmetries of CKM matrices to establish the desired equality through a series of logical simplifications.

In essence, the proof unfolds by:

1. **Defining** \( VudAbs \) as the absolute value of the `ud`th element.
2. **Applying** simplification rules to transform \( VudAbs \) into \( VAbs 0 0 \).
3. **Confirming** equivalence by aligning the transformed expression with the target \( VAbs 0 0 \).

This approach efficiently demonstrates that the absolute value of the `ud`th element in the specified CKM matrix equivalence class is indeed \( VAbs 0 0 \), as required.

/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simp]
def phaseShiftMatrix (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.mk_one, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',
    cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, star_def, ← exp_conj,
    _root_.map_mul, conj_I, conj_ofReal, neg_mul, ofReal_neg, mul_neg, Fin.mk_one, cons_val_one,
    head_fin_const, star_zero, head_cons, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd,
    tail_val', head_val', tail_cons, Fin.reduceFinMk, map_eq_zero]
  · rfl
  · rfl

/-- The multiple of two phase shift matrices is equal to the phase shift matrix with
  added phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_mul (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, mul_apply, cons_val', empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, cons_val_zero, vecCons_const, Fin.sum_univ_three, cons_val_one, head_cons,
    head_fin_const, mul_zero, add_zero, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons,
    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the unitary matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ⟨phaseShiftMatrix a b c,
  by
    rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
    change _ * (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = 1
    rw [phaseShiftMatrix_star, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← phaseShiftMatrix_one]
    simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, add_neg_cancel, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]⟩

/-- The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
  phase-shift matrix. -/
lemma phaseShift_coe_matrix (a b c : ℝ) : ↑(phaseShift a b c) = phaseShiftMatrix a b c := rfl

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix]
  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is an equivalence relation. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

/-- Two CKM matrices are equal if their underlying unitary matrices are equal. -/
lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

/-- The `ud`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ud_element) "[" V "]ud" => V.1 0 0

/-- The `us`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := us_element) "[" V "]us" => V.1 0 1

/-- The `ub`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ub_element) "[" V "]ub" => V.1 0 2

/-- The `cd`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cd_element) "[" V "]cd" => V.1 1 0

/-- The `cs`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cs_element) "[" V "]cs" => V.1 1 1

/-- The `cb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cb_element) "[" V "]cb" => V.1 1 2

/-- The `td`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := td_element) "[" V "]td" => V.1 2 0

/-- The `ts`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ts_element) "[" V "]ts" => V.1 2 1

/-- The `tb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := tb_element) "[" V "]tb" => V.1 2 2

/-- The setoid of CKM matrices defined by phase shifts of fermions. -/
instance CKMMatrixSetoid : Setoid CKMMatrix := ⟨PhaseShiftRelation, phaseShiftRelation_equiv⟩

/-- The matrix obtained from `V` by shifting the phases of the fermions. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShiftApply (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) : CKMMatrix :=
    phaseShift a b c * ↑V * phaseShift d e f

namespace phaseShiftApply

/-- A CKM matrix is equivalent to a phase-shift of itself. -/
lemma equiv (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    V ≈ phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f := by
  symm
  use a, b, c, d, e, f
  rfl

/-- The `ud` component of the CKM matrix obtained after applying a phase shift. -/
lemma ud (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f).1 0 0 = cexp (a * I + d * I) * V.1 0 0 := by
  simp only [Fin.isValue, phaseShiftApply_coe]
  rw [mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_three]
  rw [mul_apply, mul_apply, mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_three, Fin.sum_univ_three, Fin.sum_univ_three]
  simp only [Fin.isValue, cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const,
    cons_val_one, head_cons, zero_mul, add_zero, cons_val_two, tail_cons, head_fin_const, mul_zero,
    tail_val', head_val']
  change _ + _ * _ * 0 = _
  rw [exp_add]
  ring_nf

/-- The `us` component of the CKM matrix obtained after applying a phase shift. -/
lemma us (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f).1 0 1 = cexp (a * I + e * I) * V.1 0 1 := by
  exact?

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Exponential
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Trigonometric
import Mathlib.Tactic.Polyrith
/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl

    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]

    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',
    cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, star_def, ← exp_conj,
    _root_.map_mul, conj_I, conj_ofReal, neg_mul, ofReal_neg, mul_neg, Fin.mk_one, cons_val_one,
    head_fin_const, star_zero, head_cons, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd,
    tail_val', head_val', tail_cons, Fin.reduceFinMk, map_eq_zero]
  · rfl
  · rfl

/-- The multiple of two phase shift matrices is equal to the phase shift matrix with
  added phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_mul (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, mul_apply, cons_val', empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, cons_val_zero, vecCons_const, Fin.sum_univ_three, cons_val_one, head_cons,
    head_fin_const, mul_zero, add_zero, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons,
    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the unitary matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ⟨phaseShiftMatrix a b c,
  by
    rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
    change _ * (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = 1
    rw [phaseShiftMatrix_star, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← phaseShiftMatrix_one]

/-- The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
  phase-shift matrix. -/
lemma phaseShift_coe_matrix (a b c : ℝ) : ↑(phaseShift a b c) = phaseShiftMatrix a b c := rfl

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]

  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

/-- The `us`th element of the CKM matrix. -/

scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ub_element) "[" V "]ub" => V.1 0 2

/-- The `cd`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cd_element) "[" V "]cd" => V.1 1 0

/-- The `cs`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cs_element) "[" V "]cs" => V.1 1 1

/-- The `cb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cb_element) "[" V "]cb" => V.1 1 2

/-- The `td`th element of the CKM matrix. -/

/-- The `ts`th element of the CKM matrix. -/

  symm
  use a, b, c, d, e, f

  rw [mul_apply, mul_apply, mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_three, Fin.sum_univ_three, Fin.sum_univ_three]
  simp only [Fin.isValue, cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const,
    cons_val_one, head_cons, zero_mul, add_zero, cons_val_two, tail_cons, head_fin_const, mul_zero,
    tail_val', head_val']
  change _ + _ * _ * 0 = _
  rw [exp_add]
  ring_nf

    (phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f).1 0 1 = cexp (a * I + e * I) * V.1 0 1 := by

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Exponential
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Trigonometric
import Mathlib.Tactic.Polyrith
/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simp]
def phaseShiftMatrix (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.mk_one, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',
    cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, star_def, ← exp_conj,
    _root_.map_mul, conj_I, conj_ofReal, neg_mul, ofReal_neg, mul_neg, Fin.mk_one, cons_val_one,
    head_fin_const, star_zero, head_cons, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd,
    tail_val', head_val', tail_cons, Fin.reduceFinMk, map_eq_zero]
  · rfl
  · rfl

/-- The multiple of two phase shift matrices is equal to the phase shift matrix with
  added phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_mul (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, mul_apply, cons_val', empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, cons_val_zero, vecCons_const, Fin.sum_univ_three, cons_val_one, head_cons,
    head_fin_const, mul_zero, add_zero, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons,
    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the unitary matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ⟨phaseShiftMatrix a b c,
  by
    rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
    change _ * (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = 1
    rw [phaseShiftMatrix_star, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← phaseShiftMatrix_one]
    simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, add_neg_cancel, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]⟩

/-- The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
  phase-shift matrix. -/
lemma phaseShift_coe_matrix (a b c : ℝ) : ↑(phaseShift a b c) = phaseShiftMatrix a b c := rfl

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix]
  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is an equivalence relation. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

/-- Two CKM matrices are equal if their underlying unitary matrices are equal. -/
lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

/-- The `ud`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ud_element) "[" V "]ud" => V.1 0 0

/-- The `us`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := us_element) "[" V "]us" => V.1 0 1

/-- The `ub`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ub_element) "[" V "]ub" => V.1 0 2

/-- The `cd`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cd_element) "[" V "]cd" => V.1 1 0

/-- The `cs`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cs_element) "[" V "]cs" => V.1 1 1

/-- The `cb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cb_element) "[" V "]cb" => V.1 1 2

/-- The `td`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := td_element) "[" V "]td" => V.1 2 0

/-- The `ts`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ts_element) "[" V "]ts" => V.1 2 1

/-- The `tb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := tb_element) "[" V "]tb" => V.1 2 2

/-- The setoid of CKM matrices defined by phase shifts of fermions. -/
instance CKMMatrixSetoid : Setoid CKMMatrix := ⟨PhaseShiftRelation, phaseShiftRelation_equiv⟩

/-- The matrix obtained from `V` by shifting the phases of the fermions. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShiftApply (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) : CKMMatrix :=
    phaseShift a b c * ↑V * phaseShift d e f

namespace phaseShiftApply

    V ≈ phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f := by
  symm
  use a, b, c, d, e, f
  rfl

    (phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f).1 0 0 = cexp (a * I + d * I) * V.1 0 0 := by
  exact?

/-- Simplification procedure for ensuring `Fin n` literals are normalized. -/
builtin_dsimproc [simp, seval] isValue ((OfNat.ofNat _ : Fin _)) := fun e => do
  let_expr OfNat.ofNat _ m _ ← e | return .continue
  let some ⟨n, v⟩ ← getFinValue? e | return .continue
  let some m ← getNatValue? m | return .continue
  if m < n then
    -- Design decision: should we return `.continue` instead of `.done` when simplifying.
    -- In the symbolic evaluator, we must return `.done`, otherwise it will unfold the `OfNat.ofNat`
    return .done e
  return .done <| toExpr v

rag.content:
/-- A function `f` is an absolute value if it is nonnegative, zero only at 0, additive, and
multiplicative.

See also the type `AbsoluteValue` which represents a bundled version of absolute values.
-/
class IsAbsoluteValue {S} [OrderedSemiring S] {R} [Semiring R] (f : R → S) : Prop where
  /-- The absolute value is nonnegative -/
  abv_nonneg' : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x
  /-- The absolute value is positive definitive -/
  abv_eq_zero' : ∀ {x}, f x = 0 ↔ x = 0
  /-- The absolute value satisfies the triangle inequality -/
  abv_add' : ∀ x y, f (x + y) ≤ f x + f y
  /-- The absolute value is multiplicative -/
  abv_mul' : ∀ x y, f (x * y) = f x * f y

informal_statement: If two CKM matrices are equivalent under phase shifts, then their absolute values are identical.
informal_proof:
Consider two equivalent CKM matrices, denoted as \( V \) and \( U \), related by phase shifts. By definition, each element of \( U \) is obtained by multiplying the corresponding element of \( V \) by a phase factor, which is a complex number of unit magnitude.

The absolute value of a CKM matrix is determined by the sum of the squared magnitudes of its elements. Since phase shifts multiply each element by a complex number of magnitude 1, the magnitude of each element remains unchanged. Consequently, the sum of the squared magnitudes, which defines the absolute value of the matrix, remains the same for both \( V \) and \( U \).

Therefore, if two CKM matrices are equivalent under phase shifts, their absolute values are identical because the phase shifts do not alter the magnitudes of the matrix elements involved in the absolute value calculation.

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Exponential
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Trigonometric
import Mathlib.Tactic.Polyrith
/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simp]
def phaseShiftMatrix (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.mk_one, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',
    cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, star_def, ← exp_conj,
    _root_.map_mul, conj_I, conj_ofReal, neg_mul, ofReal_neg, mul_neg, Fin.mk_one, cons_val_one,
    head_fin_const, star_zero, head_cons, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd,
    tail_val', head_val', tail_cons, Fin.reduceFinMk, map_eq_zero]
  · rfl
  · rfl

/-- The multiple of two phase shift matrices is equal to the phase shift matrix with
  added phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_mul (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, mul_apply, cons_val', empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, cons_val_zero, vecCons_const, Fin.sum_univ_three, cons_val_one, head_cons,
    head_fin_const, mul_zero, add_zero, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons,
    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the unitary matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ⟨phaseShiftMatrix a b c,
  by
    rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
    change _ * (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = 1
    rw [phaseShiftMatrix_star, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← phaseShiftMatrix_one]
    simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, add_neg_cancel, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]⟩

/-- The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
  phase-shift matrix. -/
lemma phaseShift_coe_matrix (a b c : ℝ) : ↑(phaseShift a b c) = phaseShiftMatrix a b c := rfl

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix]
  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is an equivalence relation. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

/-- Two CKM matrices are equal if their underlying unitary matrices are equal. -/
lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

/-- The `ud`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ud_element) "[" V "]ud" => V.1 0 0

/-- The `us`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := us_element) "[" V "]us" => V.1 0 1

/-- The `ub`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ub_element) "[" V "]ub" => V.1 0 2

/-- The `cd`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cd_element) "[" V "]cd" => V.1 1 0

/-- The `cs`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cs_element) "[" V "]cs" => V.1 1 1

/-- The `cb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cb_element) "[" V "]cb" => V.1 1 2

/-- The `td`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := td_element) "[" V "]td" => V.1 2 0

/-- The `ts`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ts_element) "[" V "]ts" => V.1 2 1

/-- The `tb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := tb_element) "[" V "]tb" => V.1 2 2

/-- The setoid of CKM matrices defined by phase shifts of fermions. -/
instance CKMMatrixSetoid : Setoid CKMMatrix := ⟨PhaseShiftRelation, phaseShiftRelation_equiv⟩

/-- The matrix obtained from `V` by shifting the phases of the fermions. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShiftApply (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) : CKMMatrix :=
    phaseShift a b c * ↑V * phaseShift d e f

namespace phaseShiftApply

/-- A CKM matrix is equivalent to a phase-shift of itself. -/
lemma equiv (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    V ≈ phaseShiftApply V a b c d e f := by
  exact?

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Exponential
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Trigonometric
import Mathlib.Tactic.Polyrith
/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simp]
def phaseShiftMatrix (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.mk_one, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',
    cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, star_def, ← exp_conj,
    _root_.map_mul, conj_I, conj_ofReal, neg_mul, ofReal_neg, mul_neg, Fin.mk_one, cons_val_one,
    head_fin_const, star_zero, head_cons, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd,
    tail_val', head_val', tail_cons, Fin.reduceFinMk, map_eq_zero]
  · rfl
  · rfl

/-- The multiple of two phase shift matrices is equal to the phase shift matrix with
  added phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_mul (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, mul_apply, cons_val', empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, cons_val_zero, vecCons_const, Fin.sum_univ_three, cons_val_one, head_cons,
    head_fin_const, mul_zero, add_zero, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons,
    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the unitary matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ⟨phaseShiftMatrix a b c,
  by
    rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
    change _ * (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = 1
    rw [phaseShiftMatrix_star, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← phaseShiftMatrix_one]
    simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, add_neg_cancel, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]⟩

/-- The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
  phase-shift matrix. -/
lemma phaseShift_coe_matrix (a b c : ℝ) : ↑(phaseShift a b c) = phaseShiftMatrix a b c := rfl

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix]
  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is an equivalence relation. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

/-- Two CKM matrices are equal if their underlying unitary matrices are equal. -/
lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

/-- The `ud`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ud_element) "[" V "]ud" => V.1 0 0

/-- The `us`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := us_element) "[" V "]us" => V.1 0 1

/-- The `ub`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ub_element) "[" V "]ub" => V.1 0 2

/-- The `cd`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cd_element) "[" V "]cd" => V.1 1 0

/-- The `cs`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cs_element) "[" V "]cs" => V.1 1 1

/-- The `cb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cb_element) "[" V "]cb" => V.1 1 2

/-- The `td`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := td_element) "[" V "]td" => V.1 2 0

/-- The `ts`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ts_element) "[" V "]ts" => V.1 2 1

/-- The `tb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := tb_element) "[" V "]tb" => V.1 2 2

/-- The setoid of CKM matrices defined by phase shifts of fermions. -/
instance CKMMatrixSetoid : Setoid CKMMatrix := ⟨PhaseShiftRelation, phaseShiftRelation_equiv⟩

/-- The matrix obtained from `V` by shifting the phases of the fermions. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShiftApply (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) : CKMMatrix := by exact?

theorem prod_eq_mul {s : Finset α} {f : α → β} (a b : α) (hn : a ≠ b)
    (h₀ : ∀ c ∈ s, c ≠ a ∧ c ≠ b → f c = 1) (ha : a ∉ s → f a = 1) (hb : b ∉ s → f b = 1) :
    ∏ x ∈ s, f x = f a * f b := by

  · rw [hb h₂, mul_one]

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Exponential
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Trigonometric
import Mathlib.Tactic.Polyrith
/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simp]
def phaseShiftMatrix (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.mk_one, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',
    cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, star_def, ← exp_conj,
    _root_.map_mul, conj_I, conj_ofReal, neg_mul, ofReal_neg, mul_neg, Fin.mk_one, cons_val_one,
    head_fin_const, star_zero, head_cons, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd,
    tail_val', head_val', tail_cons, Fin.reduceFinMk, map_eq_zero]
  · rfl
  · rfl

/-- The multiple of two phase shift matrices is equal to the phase shift matrix with
  added phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_mul (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, mul_apply, cons_val', empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, cons_val_zero, vecCons_const, Fin.sum_univ_three, cons_val_one, head_cons,
    head_fin_const, mul_zero, add_zero, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons,
    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the unitary matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ⟨phaseShiftMatrix a b c,
  by
    rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
    change _ * (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = 1
    rw [phaseShiftMatrix_star, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← phaseShiftMatrix_one]
    simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, add_neg_cancel, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]⟩

/-- The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
  phase-shift matrix. -/
lemma phaseShift_coe_matrix (a b c : ℝ) : ↑(phaseShift a b c) = phaseShiftMatrix a b c := rfl

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix]
  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is an equivalence relation. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

/-- Two CKM matrices are equal if their underlying unitary matrices are equal. -/
lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

/-- The `ud`th element of the CKM matrix. -/

/-- The `us`th element of the CKM matrix. -/

/-- The `ub`th element of the CKM matrix. -/

/-- The `cd`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cd_element) "[" V "]cd" => V.1 1 0

/-- The `cs`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cs_element) "[" V "]cs" => V.1 1 1

/-- The `cb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cb_element) "[" V "]cb" => V.1 1 2

/-- The `td`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := td_element) "[" V "]td" => V.1 2 0

/-- The `ts`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ts_element) "[" V "]ts" => V.1 2 1

/-- The `tb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := tb_element) "[" V "]tb" => V.1 2 2

/-- The setoid of CKM matrices defined by phase shifts of fermions. -/
instance CKMMatrixSetoid : Setoid CKMMatrix := ⟨PhaseShiftRelation, phaseShiftRelation_equiv⟩

/-- The matrix obtained from `V` by shifting the phases of the fermions. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShiftApply (V : CKMMatrix) (a b c d e f : ℝ) : CKMMatrix := by exact?

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix]
  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is an equivalence relation. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

/-- Two CKM matrices are equal if their underlying unitary matrices are equal. -/
lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

informal_statement: After applying a phase shift to the CKM matrix, the specific component located at position (2,1) becomes equal to the exponential of a combination of imaginary unit terms, specifically $c$ and $e$, multiplied by the original value of the component at position (2,1) in the unshifted matrix.
informal_proof:
First, we consider the CKM matrix \( V \) before any phase shift is applied. The phase shift is represented by the operation \( \text{phaseShiftApply} \), which modifies the matrix by applying complex rotations to its elements. Specifically, the phase shift affects the individual components of the matrix through multiplication by complex exponentials.

The key aspect of this transformation is that each phase shift can be represented as multiplication by \( c\exp(I) + e\exp(I) \), where \( c \) and \( e \) are real parameters determining the magnitude and direction of the shift, respectively. When applied to the component \( V_{21} \), this multiplication results in a rotation in the complex plane, effectively changing its phase.

By examining the structure of the CKM matrix and the nature of phase shifts, we can see that the phase shift operation does not alter the magnitude of the components but only their phase angles. Thus, the new component \( (\text{phaseShiftApply}(V, a, b, c, d, e, f))_{21} \) retains the original magnitude \( V_{21} \), but its phase is adjusted by the cumulative effect of the parameters \( c \) and \( e \).

Applying the properties of complex exponentials and matrix multiplication, we can express the transformed component as:
\[
(\text{phaseShiftApply}(V, a, b, c, d, e, f))_{21} = c\exp(I) + e\exp(I) \cdot V_{21}
\]
This equation confirms that the phase-shifted component retains the original value \( V_{21} \), scaled by the phase factor \( c\exp(I) + e\exp(I) \), thereby altering only its phase and not its magnitude.

Therefore, the application of the phase shift to the CKM matrix results in the specified transformation of the component \( (2,1) \), as required.

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Exponential
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Trigonometric
import Mathlib.Tactic.Polyrith
/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simp]
def phaseShiftMatrix (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.mk_one, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',
    cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, star_def, ← exp_conj,
    _root_.map_mul, conj_I, conj_ofReal, neg_mul, ofReal_neg, mul_neg, Fin.mk_one, cons_val_one,
    head_fin_const, star_zero, head_cons, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd,
    tail_val', head_val', tail_cons, Fin.reduceFinMk, map_eq_zero]
  · rfl
  · rfl

/-- The multiple of two phase shift matrices is equal to the phase shift matrix with
  added phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_mul (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, mul_apply, cons_val', empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, cons_val_zero, vecCons_const, Fin.sum_univ_three, cons_val_one, head_cons,
    head_fin_const, mul_zero, add_zero, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons,
    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the unitary matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ⟨phaseShiftMatrix a b c,
  by
    rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
    change _ * (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = 1
    rw [phaseShiftMatrix_star, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← phaseShiftMatrix_one]
    simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, add_neg_cancel, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]⟩

/-- The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
  phase-shift matrix. -/
lemma phaseShift_coe_matrix (a b c : ℝ) : ↑(phaseShift a b c) = phaseShiftMatrix a b c := rfl

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix]
  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is an equivalence relation. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

/-- Two CKM matrices are equal if their underlying unitary matrices are equal. -/
lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

/-- The `ub`th element of the CKM matrix. -/

/-- The `cd`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cd_element) "[" V "]cd" => V.1 1 0

/-- The `cs`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cs_element) "[" V "]cs" => V.1 1 1

/-- The `cb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cb_element) "[" V "]cb" => V.1 1 2

/-- The `td`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := td_element) "[" V "]td" => V.1 2 0

/-- The `ts`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := ts_element) "[" V "]ts" => V.1 2 1

/-- The `tb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := tb_element) "[" V "]tb" => V.1 2 2

/-- The setoid of CKM matrices defined by phase shifts of fermions. -/
instance CKMMatrixSetoid : Setoid CKMMatrix := by exact?

Through a series of simplifications and rewrites, we demonstrate that this modified \( td \) component equals \( \exp(c \cdot i + d \cdot i) \) multiplied by the original \( V_{td} \) value. 

Specifically, we first resolve the definitions of the phase shift and the CKM matrix components. Then, we systematically apply these definitions to rewrite the expression, ensuring that each step maintains the equality. We conclude that the phase-shifted \( td \) component indeed simplifies to the stated exponential expression multiplied by the original \( V_{td} \).

import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Exponential
import Mathlib.Data.Complex.Trigonometric
import Mathlib.Tactic.Polyrith
/-!
# The CKM Matrix

The definition of the type of CKM matrices as unitary $3×3$-matrices.

An equivalence relation on CKM matrices is defined, where two matrices are equivalent if they are
related by phase shifts.

The notation `[V]ud` etc can be used for the elements of a CKM matrix, and
`[V]ud|us` etc for the ratios of elements.

-/

open Matrix Complex

noncomputable section

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the complex matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simp]
def phaseShiftMatrix (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

/-- The phase shift matrix for zero-phases is the identity. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_one : phaseShiftMatrix 0 0 0 = 1 := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j
  any_goals rfl
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.mk_one, Fin.isValue,
    cons_val', cons_val_one, head_cons, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, one_apply_eq]
  · simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero, Fin.reduceFinMk, cons_val',
    Fin.isValue, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons, head_cons, empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, head_fin_const, one_apply_eq]

/-- The conjugate transpose of the phase shift matrix is the phase-shift matrix
  with negated phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_star (a b c : ℝ) :
    (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = phaseShiftMatrix (- a) (- b) (- c) := by
  funext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, conjTranspose_apply, cons_val',
    cons_val_zero, empty_val', cons_val_fin_one, vecCons_const, star_def, ← exp_conj,
    _root_.map_mul, conj_I, conj_ofReal, neg_mul, ofReal_neg, mul_neg, Fin.mk_one, cons_val_one,
    head_fin_const, star_zero, head_cons, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd,
    tail_val', head_val', tail_cons, Fin.reduceFinMk, map_eq_zero]
  · rfl
  · rfl

/-- The multiple of two phase shift matrices is equal to the phase shift matrix with
  added phases. -/
lemma phaseShiftMatrix_mul (a b c d e f : ℝ) :
    phaseShiftMatrix a b c * phaseShiftMatrix d e f = phaseShiftMatrix (a + d) (b + e) (c + f) := by
  ext i j
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, Fin.zero_eta, Fin.isValue, mul_apply, cons_val', empty_val',
    cons_val_fin_one, cons_val_zero, vecCons_const, Fin.sum_univ_three, cons_val_one, head_cons,
    head_fin_const, mul_zero, add_zero, cons_val_two, Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.reduceAdd, tail_cons,
    tail_val', head_val', zero_mul, ofReal_add, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, zero_add]
  any_goals rw [mul_add, exp_add]
  change cexp (I * ↑c) * 0 = 0
  simp

/-- Given three real numbers `a b c` the unitary matrix with `exp (I * a)` etc on the
leading diagonal. -/
@[simps!]
def phaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ :=
  ⟨phaseShiftMatrix a b c,
  by
    rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
    change _ * (phaseShiftMatrix a b c)ᴴ = 1
    rw [phaseShiftMatrix_star, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← phaseShiftMatrix_one]
    simp only [phaseShiftMatrix, add_neg_cancel, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]⟩

/-- The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
  phase-shift matrix. -/
lemma phaseShift_coe_matrix (a b c : ℝ) : ↑(phaseShift a b c) = phaseShiftMatrix a b c := rfl

/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is reflective. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_refl (U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : PhaseShiftRelation U U := by
  use 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_zero, mul_zero, exp_zero]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_one]
  simp only [one_mul, mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is symmetric. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_symm {U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V U := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, h⟩ := h
  use (- a), (- b), (- c), (- e), (- f), (- g)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val]
  rw [h]
  repeat rw [mul_assoc]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix, ofReal_neg, mul_neg]
  rw [phaseShiftMatrix_mul]
  repeat rw [← mul_assoc]
  simp only [phaseShiftMatrix_mul, neg_add_cancel, phaseShiftMatrix_one, one_mul, add_neg_cancel,
    mul_one]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is transitive. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PhaseShiftRelation U V → PhaseShiftRelation V W → PhaseShiftRelation U W := by
  intro hUV hVW
  obtain ⟨a, b, c, e, f, g, hUV⟩ := hUV
  obtain ⟨d, i, j, k, l, m, hVW⟩ := hVW
  use (a + d), (b + i), (c + j), (e + k), (f + l), (g + m)
  rw [Subtype.ext_iff_val, hUV, hVW]
  simp only [Submonoid.coe_mul, phaseShift_coe_matrix]
  rw [mul_assoc, mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, phaseShiftMatrix_mul,
    add_comm k e, add_comm l f, add_comm m g]

/-- The relation `PhaseShiftRelation` is an equivalence relation. -/
lemma phaseShiftRelation_equiv : Equivalence PhaseShiftRelation where
  refl := phaseShiftRelation_refl
  symm := phaseShiftRelation_symm
  trans := phaseShiftRelation_trans

/-- The type of CKM matrices. -/
def CKMMatrix : Type := unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

/-- Two CKM matrices are equal if their underlying unitary matrices are equal. -/
lemma CKMMatrix_ext {U V : CKMMatrix} (h : U.val = V.val) : U = V := by
  cases U
  cases V
  subst h
  rfl

/-- The `cs`th element of the CKM matrix. -/
scoped[CKMMatrix] notation (name := cs_element) "[" V "]cs" => V.1 1 1

/-- The `cb`th element of the CKM matrix. -/

leading diagonal. -/

  ![![cexp (I * a), 0, 0], ![0, cexp (I * b), 0], ![0, 0, cexp (I * c)]]

  added phases. -/

C0_dependencies.name: PhaseShiftRelation
C0_dependencies.content:
/-- The relation on unitary matrices (CKM matrices) satisfied if two unitary matrices
  are related by phase shifts of quarks. -/
def PhaseShiftRelation (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c e f g, U = phaseShift a b c * V * phaseShift e f g

theorem exp_sum {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (f : α → ℂ) :
    exp (∑ x ∈ s, f x) = ∏ x ∈ s, exp (f x) :=
